GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: The discussion started with two Astra presets and expanded, with explicit user authorization, to the workflow that makes those presets useful. The user currently chooses single-session on every model because the tracked workflow is rigid and slow. The desired optimization is fewer expensive Astra implementation turns and fewer slow independent-review barriers, not maximum delegation or the lowest total token count across all providers.

Alternatives.Alternative: Keep balanced unchanged and only add model presets. Rejected as an exact solution: balanced makes delegation optional, and tracked vv-implementer results still require independent reviewers before close.

Use orchestrated with a stronger no-edit prompt. Insufficient: the engine still requires a non-empty reviewer set and moves each successful implementer result to awaiting_reviews. A prompt cannot supply a missing controller-acceptance transition.
Weaken orchestrated globally or allow an empty requiredReviewers array to mean success. Rejected because it changes existing obligations and loses an explicit, auditable acceptance event.

Group many plan tasks into one existing strict work item. This can reduce reviews today, but it does not provide the user's requested primary-session acceptance between separately dispatched tasks within that group.
Use GPT-5.6 Sol for independent review. Rejected by the user because the reviewer should add a different model-family perspective from Astra.

Use GLM-5.3 Flash to make every-task reviews cheaper. Superseded by the user's priorities: their GLM token cost is not the bottleneck, review should be less frequent, and the observed provider throughput did not establish a substantial Flash advantage.

Implement fully automatic parallel scheduling, isolated writer worktrees, and asynchronous review. Deferred because they add coordination and snapshot complexity before the simpler delegated acceptance loop has been evaluated.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Exact workflow tool names, discriminated input shapes, persistence versioning, and checkpoint snapshot representation belong in the implementation design derived from the approved specification. They must preserve the explicit authorization, attempt binding, invalidation, and legacy compatibility requirements.

Actual wall-clock benefit, Astra usage reduction, Spark reliability as Guardian, and GLM review precision require controlled model runs. No provider calls were made during the discussion, and catalog membership does not prove account access.

If Spark is unsuitable for Guardian or small_model, revisit separate per-agent fast assignments with the user. Do not silently widen this change into a role-system redesign or silently fall back to Luna.

A hard technical prohibition on all controller source writes is not part of the first version. Merely hiding an edit tool would not prevent shell-based writes and must not be marketed as a security boundary.

The pre-existing installed GRACE CLI diagnostic discrepancy must be resolved or receive an explicit user disposition before execution. Investigating or fixing the external CLI is separate from this product change; archived plans must remain immutable.

Scenarios.Scenario: A twenty-task implementation plan uses primary-session acceptance after each worker, code review after two meaningful milestones, and final spec plus code review. This yields four initial independent reviewer launches, not forty. Corrective review remains bounded and evidence-driven.

A worker fixes its own lint/type/test failures within its assigned task and returns once it has a coherent result. Astra reads the material changed code and evidence, accepts it, and dispatches the next task without an independent reviewer barrier.
A task exposes an architectural ambiguity. The worker returns NEEDS_CONTEXT; Astra or the user resolves the decision. The same stopped work item is not reset or silently redispatched.

A code checkpoint passes, but a later planned task changes its covered contract. Earlier review remains historical evidence for its snapshot, not approval of the new revision. Subsequent milestones and the final gate cover the later changes without automatically rerunning all historical reviews. Content changed during an in-flight review instead makes that review stale for the current barrier.

A review_only work item closes after FAIL as a completed findings report. The plan's checkpoint remains failed, so delegated execution cannot report final completion by checking only that the work item is closed.

A legacy orchestrated plan and its persisted strict work items are loaded after upgrade. They keep their required reviewers and original close gates rather than receiving controller acceptance implicitly.

The new presets are present after managed preset refresh, but sync does not activate either preset or change the user's current single-session assignment. Applying a preset and restarting are separate explicit operations.

Repository alias limits intentionally distinguish pricing/compaction boundaries from raw capability.

https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news260910/ and https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode identify deepseek-flash as V4.1 Flash and document low/high/max with high as the API default. New presets should not use the retired V4 alias as their canonical ID.

https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-5.3 documents the full text-only model, low/high/max effort with max as default, and its complex software-engineering focus. Full GLM high is a starting review configuration, not a demonstrated optimal reviewer.

https://openai.com/index/introducing-gpt-5-3-codex-spark/ describes 128K context, text-only input, research-preview quota separation, and a vendor claim above 1000 output tokens per second. https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents provides a read-only Spark medium explorer example.

OpenCode 1.18.30 catalog inspection showed the proposed base model IDs and medium/high/max variants where selected. Its Spark metadata also advertised image/PDF input and none effort beyond the cited public description; new aliases must be conservative rather than inheriting unsupported capability claims.

OpenRouter provider-specific pages observed on 2026-09-11 showed DeepSeek V4.1 Flash around 122 tokens/second at DeepSeek, Qwen3.8 Flash around 44 at Alibaba Cloud International, GLM-5.3 Flash around 33 at Z.ai, and full GLM-5.3 around 31 at Z.ai. These are mixed-workload provider snapshots, not measurements of the user's subscription endpoints or of complete tasks.

https://openai.com/business/guides-and-resources/a-practical-guide-to-building-ai-agents/ describes manager-worker orchestration, bounded responsibilities, and optimizing cost/latency against a quality baseline. https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system discusses coordination overhead, concise artifact references, and meaningful end-state checkpoints rather than evaluating every intermediate step.

PlanSelfReview.ReviewScope: The primary controller reviewed the completed draft plan against all thirty approved acceptance criteria, the current source contracts, actual pinned SDK shapes, the GRACE task/assertion/scope rules, and the requested latency and model-cost goals. This is self-review, not independent review or execution evidence.
PlanSelfReview.Decision: Use an additive delegated work-item mode and a separate plan-run/checkpoint registry. Reuse existing review_only work items for reviewer calls so legacy FAIL/closure semantics are not weakened.

Register obligations from the approved vvoc plan and linked spec, rather than letting a model supply an incomplete checkpoint list. This is declarative registration, not an autonomous scheduler or a change to external GRACE plan formats.
PlanSelfReview.Correction: Restrict the new control-tool schemas to the delegated startup profile so the user's existing single-session path does not pay unnecessary schema/context overhead. Keep the old profiles' policies and tool footprint unchanged.
Separate historical milestone success from current snapshot validity. A recheck of a historical milestone must not create a new barrier merely because later planned work changed a file.

Separate a final checkpoint PASS from sealing the complete run. Require explicit complete: true on a fresh final verification, preserving bounded rework before completion and rejecting rework of already sealed runs.

Cover later review findings against an already accepted task with explicit rework authorization tied to a failed checkpoint. Preserve original acceptance history and the consumed implementation-attempt budget rather than resetting the task under a new key.
Bind attempt/result handling to actual OpenCode callID and root-session metadata. Add negative tests for a child named vv-controller, stale callbacks, duplicate decisions, and I/O failures.

New target test paths are guarded with MustExist assertions because Bun can silently skip an absent path argument. The current persistence tests are in workflow.test.ts; the future standalone persistence.test.ts is explicitly a new file.
PlanSelfReview.Coverage: Every approved AC-01 through AC-30 maps to at least one task in plan.xml SpecCoverage. Twelve tasks have a true-dependency DAG, explicit literal write scope, behavior-sensitive baselines, and leaf verification commands. Durable state is reconciled centrally after observed work verifies.
PlanSelfReview.Evidence: The existing five-file baseline suite was rerun without nonexistent path arguments: 92 tests passed, 0 failed; bun run typecheck passed. Draft GRACE current-assertion and parallel-preflight lint returned zero errors and warnings before the final self-review edits; both are rerun after those edits.
PlanSelfReview.RemainingLimit: Source implementation, new regression scenarios, real model calls, completed-plan approval, explicit sequential execution selection, and disposition of the pre-existing GRACE module-health error are still outstanding. Self-review does not authorize implementation or establish runtime performance.

ExecutionAuthorization.Approval: The user replied approved after presentation of the completed plan and the requested sequential execution and diagnostic-disposition conditions. The specification and completed plan are now approved.
ExecutionAuthorization.CommitAuthorization: The user's preceding instruction explicitly authorized implementation and a subsequent commit. No push, release, credentialed model calls, or automatic GRACE apply/archive is authorized by this record.
ExecutionAuthorization.DiagnosticDisposition: The previously identified GRACE 4.0.7 module-navigation/module-health error may remain a documented limitation while execution proceeds only if the actual lint, baseline, target, final, and project test gates pass. This does not waive any new failure or permit changes to archived bundles.
ExecutionAuthorization.Portability: The plan does not require Astra as its implementation agent. Another capable primary model can execute it with the complete approved package and fresh preflight, following the host session's work policy and the agreed sequential mode. Astra is a target preset assignment, not a dependency of the implementation process.
ExecutionAuthorization.CurrentStop: No runtime implementation has begun. The user asked about model portability after approval, so the current response records approval and answers that question rather than silently starting implementation.
